title: When I reach, not when I will reach
goal: Use the present after when, as soon as, after, before and until
intro: After time words like when, as soon as, before, after and until, English uses the present tense to talk about the future: “I’ll call you when I reach.” Saying “when I will reach” is one of the most common Indian-English errors. The “will” goes only in the other half of the sentence.

examples: I’ll call you when I get home.
We’ll start as soon as he arrives.

rules.rule: Same with “if”: if + present, will + verb.
examples: If it rains, we’ll stay in.
If you need anything, I’ll be here.

rules.rule: For a finished future action, use present perfect after when.
examples: I’ll send it when I’ve finished.
You can go after you’ve eaten.

mistakes.wrong: I will call you when I will reach.
mistakes.right: I’ll call you when I reach.

mistakes.wrong: If you will come, we will go.
As soon as I will get the results, I will tell you.
mistakes.right: As soon as I get the results, I’ll tell you.
mistakes.why: After “as soon as”, use the present.

ex.q: If she ___ late, we’ll start without her.
We ___ dinner after the guests arrive.
I will tell him when he will come.
ex.fixed: I will tell him when he comes.

ex.q: Don't leave until the meeting will finish.
ex.fixed: Don't leave until the meeting finishes.

ex.q: As soon as I will get the money, I will pay you.
ex.fixed: As soon as I get the money, I will pay you.

ex.q: Call me as soon as you ___ (land).

ex.a: I will send you the photos when I get home.

ex.q: Correct this: “I will message you when I will reach.”
a: I will message you when I reach
I'll message you when I reach
I will text you when I reach
I'll text you when I reach

talk: Tell the coach your plan for tomorrow using when, after, before and as soon as: “When I wake up, I’ll…”. Keep “will” out of the time half.
